newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator expects nuke waste dump law to pass.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator expects nuke waste dump law to pass.

text.p: U.S. Senate energy committee chairman Frank Murkowski predicted Thursday that the new Congress would pass and President Clinton would sign a law to build a temporary dump for nuclear waste from power plants.

"I make this prediction based on the hope President Clinton and a new energy secretary will act responsibly and put public safety and common sense above politics," the Alaska Republican said in a statement.
Nuclear utilities have been pressing for an interim storage site to relieve them of spent fuel accumulating at their plants.

The Clinton administration has refused to back bills to build an interim site because it does not want to divert resources from constructing a permanent facility, most likely at Yucca Mountain in Nevada, due to be ready by 2010.
But under law, the government must start taking over the utilities' spent fuel in 1998.
The Senate last year passed a bill calling for an interim storage site to be built in Nevada, so the Energy Department could start taking the spent fuel in the next few years.
"We need a safe, national policy of interim storage at one site, until a permanent facility is opened," Murkowski said.
Other issues heading Murkowksi's agenda for the committee include electric utility deregulation, the future of the Energy Department, forest management reform, and National Park rehabilitation.
A committee aide said Murkowski was aiming to "rejuvenate the land management agencies...expand visitor services and recreation opportunities (on federal lands)."
Murkowski said he also planned to hold oversight hearings on global climate change negotiations and the Environmental Protection Agency's proposals for tightening smog and particulate standards.
